successCriteria.description: A cancel endpoint is registered in leaveRoutes that delegates to ILeaveService.cancel(actor, id) and returns HTTP 200 with the resulting LeaveRequest on success.
The handler resolves the actor via resolveActor(request) before invoking the service, so a missing/invalid request.user yields an UnauthorizedError at the API boundary.
Errors are routed through sendError(reply, error): AppError maps to { error, code } with its statusCode, and any non-AppError throw maps to 500.
The handler uses the single leaveService instance already resolved at the top of leaveRoutes (fastify.leaveService ?? createLeaveService()), not a new resolution.

constraints: No controller file: the route handler calls the service directly, matching the existing four endpoints in leave.routes.ts.
No service logic, no repository changes, and no tests in this phase — the cancel operation is already implemented in LeaveService (Phase 2) and is treated as a fixed contract.

The handler must mirror the existing submit/approve/reject handlers: resolveActor, destructure id from request.params, await leaveService.cancel(actor, id), reply.status(200).send(...), wrapped in try/catch with request.log.error(error) then sendError(reply, error).
The endpoint returns 200 on success (not 201), consistent with the other state-transition endpoints.
outOfScope: Implementing or modifying the cancel service logic, authorization, timing guard, balance release, audit, or notification behavior (Phase 2 deliverable).
Adding tests for the cancel endpoint or the cancel service operation (Phase 4 deliverable).
Changing src/modules/leave/index.ts or the route registration signature — leaveRoutes is already re-exported.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Actor is resolved and role-validated at the API boundary by resolveActor before the service is invoked; the service enforces cancellation authorization.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: AppError (UnauthorizedError, ForbiddenError, ConflictError, NotFoundError) surfaces as { error, code } with its statusCode; any other throw becomes 500.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The new handler must reuse the existing resolveActor and sendError helpers and follow the identical try/catch + request.log.error + reply.status(200).send pattern of the submit/approve/reject handlers.
The handler must call the ILeaveService.cancel(actor, id) method exactly as declared, passing the resolved actor and the :id path parameter.
The service instance must be resolved once as fastify.leaveService ?? createLeaveService(), matching the existing endpoints' resolution.

integrationPoints.why: The route delegates the entire cancel operation to the already-implemented service method.
Reused for API-boundary authentication and error mapping, keeping the new endpoint consistent with existing ones.
